raw_text:
Below is a structured 12-week plan designed for fat loss and improved glycaemic control for a 45-year-old female with type 2 diabetes (on metformin, HbA1c 7.2). It includes phased training, weekly session details, and a clear, diabetes-appropriate nutrition plan with monitoring, recovery, and safety guidance. Assumes medical clearance and stable metformin dosing. Encourage coordination with her physician, especially if medications change as weight and glycaemia improve.

Overall structure
- Frequency: 4 training days/week (2 full-body strength, 1 metabolic conditioning + core, 1 low-impact cardio/conditioning), plus optional light activity (walking) most days.
- Phases:
  1) Foundation and insulin sensitivity (Weeks 1–4)
  2) Progressive overload and metabolic conditioning (Weeks 5–8)
  3) Intensification and consolidation (Weeks 9–12)
- Monitoring:
  - Pre- and post-exercise capillary glucose for first 2–3 weeks and after any training progression until stable. Target pre-exercise 100–180 mg/dL (5.6–10 mmol/L). Avoid starting <90 mg/dL (5 mmol/L). If <90, take 10–15 g fast-acting carbs; recheck in 15 min. If >250 mg/dL (13.9 mmol/L), hydrate, perform easier low-intensity cardio; if symptomatic/ketones positive (if she checks), defer and contact clinician.
  - Carry 15–20 g fast-acting carbohydrate (glucose tabs/gel) during sessions.
  - Hydration: 2–3 L water/day; 500 ml during training hour.
- RPE targets: mostly 6–8/10 for work sets; cardio at 5–7/10 unless noted.

Nutrition strategy (consistent through 12 weeks, with small adjustments)
- Energy: Set modest deficit of ~20% below maintenance to promote 0.5–0.75% bodyweight loss/week. Estimate TDEE (e.g., 1800–2000 kcal typical for many women this age/size; calculate precisely from her stats). Example starting intake: 1500–1600 kcal/day; adjust by 100–150 kcal every 2 weeks based on weight trend (aim 0.4–0.7 kg/week).
- Macronutrients:
  - Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day to preserve lean mass and improve satiety (e.g., 100–130 g for 60–65 kg; scale to actual weight).
  - Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day, prioritizing mono- and polyunsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, seeds, avocado, oily fish). Limit saturated fat.
  - Carbohydrate: Fill remainder (typically 90–140 g/day at 1500–1600 kcal). Distribute evenly and pair with protein/fat/fiber to blunt glycaemic spikes.
- Carbohydrate timing and distribution:
  - 3 main meals + 1–2 snacks. Aim 25–35 g net carbs per meal, 10–15 g per snack.
  - Place a slightly higher carb portion pre- and post-exercise (e.g., 25–35 g low-GI carbs 60–90 min pre-workout; 20–30 g carbs + 20–30 g protein within 1–2 hours after).
  - Choose low to moderate GI sources: oats, quinoa, brown/wild rice (measured portions), legumes, berries, apples/pears, Greek yogurt (unsweetened), milk/kefir, high-fiber wraps, sweet potato (150 g), non-starchy vegetables.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day from vegetables, legumes, chia/flax, berries. Increase gradually to avoid GI distress.
- Micronutrients:
  - Emphasize magnesium (nuts, legumes, leafy greens), potassium (leafy greens, avocado), omega-3s (2–3 oily fish meals/week or 1–2 g EPA/DHA supplement if approved).
  - Vitamin D status: check with clinician; supplement if deficient.
- Glycaemic-friendly meal templates (examples)
  - Breakfast options (25–35 g carbs, 30 g protein):
    - Greek yogurt (200 g) + whey (15 g) + 60 g berries + 15 g walnuts; 1 slice high-fiber toast.
    - Veggie omelet (3 eggs/egg whites mix) + 1 small apple + 1 tsp peanut butter.
    - Oats (40 g dry) cooked with milk; add 25 g whey, cinnamon, chia seeds.
  - Lunch options (25–35 g carbs, 30–40 g protein):
    - Grilled chicken salad: 120–150 g chicken, mixed greens, chickpeas (80 g), olive oil–lemon dressing.
    - Tuna bowl: 120 g tuna, 100 g quinoa, cucumber, tomato, olives, feta.
  - Dinner options (25–35 g carbs, 30–40 g protein):
    - Salmon (150 g), 150 g sweet potato, roasted broccoli + olive oil.
    - Lean turkey chili with beans, side salad; optional 1 small high-fiber wrap.
  - Snacks (10–15 g carbs, 15–25 g protein):
    - Cottage cheese + cinnamon + ½ pear
    - Protein shake + 10 almonds
    - Edamame with sea salt
- Foods to limit/avoid:
  - Sugary drinks/juices, refined sweets, large portions of white bread/pasta/rice, high-fat fried foods.
  - Alcohol: if consumed, limit to 1 drink or less/week; avoid around training; note alcohol can increase delayed hypoglycaemia.
- Meal timing and meds:
  - Metformin is generally weight-neutral and low hypoglycaemia risk; still monitor during new exercise.
  - Consistent mealtimes help glycaemic control; avoid long fasting initially. If trying time-restricted eating, start only after Weeks 4–6 when responses are known, and coordinate with clinician.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: 7–9 hours; consistent schedule. Reduce late caffeine.
- Daily steps: 7,000–10,000+, with post-meal walks of 10–15 min to blunt glucose spikes.
- Stress: 5–10 min/day breathing, mindfulness, or light mobility.

Strength and cardio training plan
- Warm-up each session (8–10 min):
  - 5 min brisk walk/cycle/elliptical
  - Dynamic mobility: ankle rocks, hip hinges, shoulder circles, thoracic rotations
  - 1–2 ramp-up sets for first two lifts
- Cool-down (5–8 min):
  - Easy cardio + breathing; light stretching for hips, quads, hamstrings, chest.

Progression principles
- Use RIR (reps in reserve): stop sets with 1–2 reps “in the tank.”
- When you can exceed top rep target on last set with good form, increase load next session (upper body +2–2.5 kg; lower body +2.5–5 kg).
- Deload in Week 9 Day 1 only via first session lighter warm-up; otherwise plan has built-in undulations.

Phase 1: Foundation and insulin sensitivity (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: Learn form, establish consistency, increase NEAT, enhance insulin sensitivity with full-body strength and low–moderate intensity cardio. RPE 6–7 mostly.

Weekly schedule template
- Day 1: Full-Body Strength A
- Day 2: Low-Impact Cardio + Core
- Day 3: Full-Body Strength B
- Day 4: Metabolic Circuit + Mobility
- Optional: 2–4 post-meal walks (10–15 min)

Week 1
- Day 1 (Strength A)
  - Goblet squat 3×8–10
  - Seated cable row 3×10–12
  - DB bench press 3×8–10
  - Hip hinge pattern: Romanian deadlift (DB) 3×8–10
  - Half-kneeling cable chop 2×10/side
  - Glute bridge 2×12–15
- Day 2 (Cardio + Core)
  - Bike or brisk incline walk 30–35 min at RPE 5–6
  - Core: Dead bug 2×8/side; Side plank 2×20–30 s/side; Pallof press 2×10/side
- Day 3 (Strength B)
  - Leg press 3×10–12
  - Lat pulldown (neutral grip) 3×8–10
  - DB overhead press 3×8–10
  - Step-up (box ~ knee height) 2×10/leg
  - Back extension or hip hinge drill 2×10–12
  - Cable face pull 2×12–15
- Day 4 (Metabolic Circuit + Mobility)
  - Circuit (3 rounds; 40 s work/20 s rest; 2 min between rounds): Kettlebell deadlift, TRX row, sled push or treadmill push, battle ropes, farmer carry (30–40 m)
  - Mobility: 5–8 min hips/thoracic

Week 2
- Repeat Week 1 structure; add 1 set to main lifts (to 4 sets) if RPE ≤7. Add 5 min to cardio day (35–40 min). Slightly increase loading if form solid.

Week 3
- Strength A/B: Move rep ranges to 6–8 on primary moves; accessories remain 10–12. Introduce split squat instead of step-up (2–3×8/leg).
- Cardio: 35–40 min with 5×1 min brisk surges at RPE 7, 2 min easy between.
- Circuit: Increase to 4 rounds or extend work to 45 s.

Week 4
- Strength: Keep 4 sets primary lifts; aim top end of reps then add load.
- Cardio: 40 min steady RPE 5–6.
- Circuit: 4 rounds; finish with 8–10 min easy spin/walk cool-down.
- End-of-phase check: bodyweight trend, waist, average fasting glucose, pre/post-exercise glucose responses, perceived energy/hunger. Adjust calories by ±100–150 if needed.

Phase 2: Progressive overload and metabolic conditioning (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: Increase strength, add intervals to improve cardiorespiratory fitness and post-exercise glucose uptake; maintain joint-friendly volume. RPE 6–8.

Weekly schedule template remains (Days 1–4).

Week 5
- Day 1 (Strength A)
  - Back squat (or continue goblet if form/comfort) 4×5–6
  - Barbell or trap-bar RDL 4×6–8
  - Bench press (BB or DB) 4×6–8
  - Chest-supported row 3×8–10
  - Farmer carry 3×40–50 m
- Day 2 (Intervals + Core)
  - Elliptical or bike intervals: 6×2 min at RPE 7 with 2 min easy between; 5 min warm-up/cool-down (total ~33–35 min)
  - Core: Stir-the-pot (Swiss ball) 3×8–10 circles/side; Side plank 3×25–35 s/side
- Day 3 (Strength B)
  - Leg press 4×8–10
  - Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up 4×6–8
  - DB overhead press 3–4×6–8
  - Bulgarian split squat 3×8/leg
  - Cable face pull 3×12–15
- Day 4 (Metabolic Complex)
  - KB complex, 4 rounds: 6 swings, 6 goblet squats, 6 push presses/arm (or DB), walk 40 m; Rest 90–120 s between rounds.
  - Finish: 10 min Zone 2 (RPE 5)

Week 6
- Progress loads 2–5%. Add 1 interval (7×2 min). Keep strength reps same; aim 1 RIR.
- Optional “glycaemic booster” walk: 10–15 min after two main meals on 3+ days this week.

Week 7
- Strength A: Shift to 5×5 on first lift (squat or goblet), others 4×6–8.
- Intervals: 8×90 s at RPE 7–8, 90 s easy.
- Metabolic day: Add sled push 2×20–30 m finisher (RPE 8, full recovery).

Week 8
- Volume consolidation: Keep loads, reduce a set on accessory lifts (–1 set) to manage fatigue.
- Cardio: One longer steady session instead of intervals: 45–50 min RPE 5–6.
- Reassess nutrition: If weight loss <0.3%/wk average and energy OK, reduce 100 kcal/day from fats or carbs; otherwise hold.

Phase 3: Intensification and consolidation (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: Maintain deficit, consolidate strength, emphasize higher-efficiency conditioning, and refine habits for long-term glycaemic control. RPE 7–8, with careful glucose monitoring on interval days.

Week 9
- Day 1 (Strength A)
  - Trap-bar deadlift 4×4–6
  - Front squat or goblet squat 4×6
  - Bench press 4×5–6
  - One-arm DB row 3×8/side
  - Weighted carry (overhead or suitcase) 3×30–40 m
- Day 2 (HIIT-lite + Core)
  - Bike: 10 min warm-up; 8 rounds 30 s hard (RPE 8) / 90 s easy; 5–8 min cool-down. Total ~30–35 min.
  - Core: Pallof press 3×10/side; Back extension 3×10–12
- Day 3 (Strength B)
  - Leg press 4×8
  - Assisted pull-up or lat pulldown 4×6–8
  - DB incline press 3×8–10
  - Reverse lunge 3×8/leg
  - Face pull 2–3×12–15
- Day 4 (Mixed conditioning)
  - Circuit (4 rounds): Row erg 250 m, KB swings 12, step-ups 10/leg, battle ropes 30 s; Rest ~90 s.
  - Finish: 5–8 min easy

Week 10
- Progress loads 2–5% where possible. Keep HIIT-lite same or add 1 round if recovery good.
- Add core anti-rotation (walkouts) 2×8 on Strength days.

Week 11
- Strength: Keep top sets at RPE 8; back-off sets (–10% load) 1–2×6–8 for first lift.
- Conditioning: Tempo intervals on elliptical: 5×3 min at RPE 7, 2 min easy.
- Add longer Zone 2 walk or cycle once this week: 50–60 min.

Week 12 (taper and test)
- Reduce total volume ~20–30% to freshen up; maintain intensity.
- Conditioning: Choose preferred modality; two sessions at RPE 6–7, 30–35 min.
- Optional performance check: AMRAP set at prior Week 9 loads (stop 1 RIR), or rep PR on goblet squat/leg press. Compare body metrics and glucose logs.

Session-specific glucose and fueling guidance
- Pre-workout (60–90 min before): Protein 20–30 g + 20–35 g low-GI carbs + a little fat/fiber. Example: small oat yogurt bowl or toast + eggs.
- If pre-exercise glucose <90 mg/dL: Take 10–15 g fast-acting carbs (e.g., 3–4 glucose tabs); recheck in 15 min before starting.
- During exercise: Water. For sessions >60–75 min and if trending low or symptomatic, take 10 g carbs.
- Post-workout (within 1–2 h): 25–35 g protein + 20–30 g carbs; include vegetables and fats at the meal to slow absorption if post-ex spikes are an issue.
- Record pre/post glucose for the first 2–3 weeks of each phase and after any major change in intensity.

Weekly nutrition check-ins and adjustments
- Weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, 10: Review 7-day average weight, waist, energy, hunger, training performance, and glucose:
  - If weight loss >1%/wk or low energy: add 100–150 kcal (mostly carbs around training or healthy fats).
  - If loss <0.3%/wk and adherence good: reduce 100–150 kcal (preferably carbs at non-training meals or fats).
  - Maintain protein; keep carbs concentrated around workouts and earlier in the day if evening spikes occur.
- Sodium/potassium balance: For heavy sweaters, include 1–2 electrolyte servings/week in hotter conditions.

Sample 1-day meal plan (approx. 1550 kcal; 120 g protein, 120 g carbs, 55 g fat)
- Breakfast: Vegetable omelet (2 eggs + 150 ml egg whites), 1 slice whole-grain toast, ½ avocado; coffee or tea (unsweetened).
- Snack: Greek yogurt (170 g) + 60 g berries + 10 g almonds.
- Lunch: Grilled chicken salad: 140 g chicken, mixed leaves, tomatoes, cucumber, 80 g chickpeas, 1 tbsp olive oil, balsamic.
- Pre-workout (if training later): Small banana or 30 g oats with whey in water (20–25 g carbs, 20 g protein).
- Dinner (post-workout): Salmon 150 g, 150 g roasted sweet potato, asparagus with 1 tsp olive oil.
- Optional evening: Cottage cheese 150 g with cinnamon.

Safety and special considerations
- Footwear and feet: Proper shoes; inspect feet daily; avoid high-impact plyometrics initially.
- Blood pressure: Monitor if hypertensive; avoid breath-holding (Valsalva).
- Retinopathy/neuropathy: If present, modify intensity and avoid high-pressure maneuvers; favor machines and supported positions as needed.
- Sick days: If unwell or glucose uncontrolled, prioritize hydration and easy walking; resume intensity when stable.

Metrics to track
- Weekly: Weight, waist, average fasting glucose, 1–2 post-prandial readings (rotate meals), perceived energy/hunger, step count.
- Training: Loads, reps, RPE; cardio durations and intervals completed.
- Outcomes expected (with adherence): 4–6% bodyweight reduction, improved cardio fitness, fasting glucose and post-prandials trending down, potential HbA1c drop by 0.5–1.0% at 3 months. Coordinate with her clinician to reassess meds if readings improve.

This plan provides a clear week-by-week training structure, carbohydrate-smart nutrition, and diabetes-specific safeguards to promote fat loss and better glycaemic control. Adjust loads and calories to her body size and weekly trends, and maintain close glucose monitoring during training progressions.
